content_voiceover: Z N F three eight four rearranged ALL has an immunophenotype that can trip up boards questions because it can masquerade as something else. These blasts characteristically show low expression of C D ten, which is unusual since most B lineage ALL is C D ten positive, and they show high expression of the myeloid markers C D thirteen and C D thirty-three. That aberrant myeloid marker expression is a classic pitfall, it can make the leukemia look like it might be mixed phenotype or even myeloid at first glance, so recognizing this pattern in the context of a B lineage ALL should raise Z N F three eight four rearrangement on your differential. In terms of partner genes, E P three hundred is the most common fusion partner at forty-three percent, followed by T C F three at thirty-one percent, with various others making up the rest. Interestingly, the specific fusion E P three hundred colon colon Z N F three eight four is associated with a lower cumulative risk of relapse and significantly better event-free survival compared to Z N F three eight four rearranged ALL with other partner genes, so even within this one rearrangement category, the partner gene carries prognostic weight.
keypoints: ZNF384-rearranged ALL: low CD10, high CD13 and CD33 expression
Aberrant myeloid marker expression can mimic mixed phenotype leukemia
Most common partner gene is EP300 (43%), then TCF3 (31%)
EP300::ZNF384 fusion carries lower relapse risk and better EFS than other partners
keypoint_voiceover: Remember the immunophenotype, low C D ten with high C D thirteen and C D thirty-three, which can mimic myeloid disease. E P three hundred is the leading partner gene, and E P three hundred colon colon Z N F three eight four specifically predicts a better outcome than other Z N F three eight four partner fusions.
